news_drafts.headline: East Dunbartonshire health and social care partnership running down reserves to cover funding shortfall
news_drafts.lead: The Health and Social Care Partnership serving East Dunbartonshire has depleted nearly a third of its general reserves in a single year to bridge a funding gap, with savings targets falling far short of what is needed. The partnership achieved only 39 per cent of its 2026/27 savings programme by month 4, a shortfall it is covering by drawing down £8.192m from reserves. General contingency reserves have fallen from £3.955m to a projected £1.290m by March 2027. The partnership explicitly warns that continued reliance on reserve drawdowns to balance budgets "may be compromised" its financial sustainability. The financial strain has forced service access restrictions: charges are rising, eligibility criteria tightening and waiting lists extending. A 3.5 per cent pay uplift for staff was approved with no corresponding funding, adding to the pressure. The partnership carried forward £3.036m in unachieved savings from previous years, which must still be realised alongside current targets.

news_drafts.headline: East Dunbartonshire underlying borrowing need to reach £785m by 2028/29, cash reserves to fall to £1.7m
news_drafts.lead: East Dunbartonshire's underlying borrowing need, the total the council has spent on long-lived assets it has not yet paid for, will grow by 39 per cent over three years to £785m by 2028/29, according to the council's treasury management strategy. The council is currently using cash balances to bridge the gap between what it owes and what it needs to borrow. However, that buffer will shrink by 94 per cent, from £27.6m to £1.7m by 2028/29, as capital spending on housing and other programmes accelerates. Once reserves are exhausted, the council will need to borrow for all new capital expenditure. The forecast reflects a sharp increase in housing investment, with Housing Revenue Account capital spending peaking at £86.4m in 2027/28, more than five times the £16m spent in 2024/25.

findings.committee: Health and Social Care Partnership Integration Joint Board
findings.paper_title: Item 18b. Appendix 2 EO Performance Audit and Risk Committee Minutes 29.06.26
findings.headline: The 2025/26 IJB unaudited annual accounts were submitted in a timely manner, and the committee commended this, with the 30 September deadline under discussion.
findings.detail: Members commended the timely submission of the 2025/26 unaudited accounts. Forvis Mazars was asked to comment on the likelihood of meeting the 30 September deadline, and proposed sharing the Annual Audit Plan by correspondence paper, with an August diary hold for another committee meeting.
findings.matters: A council on track to meet the 30 September statutory deadline, and a lender watching for audit timetable risk, would see this as the key forward milestone.
findings.quote: CS and LC commended the submission of accounts in a timely manner.

findings.committee: Health and Social Care Partnership Integration Joint Board
findings.paper_title: Item 18b. Appendix 2 EO Performance Audit and Risk Committee Minutes 29.06.26
findings.headline: The 2024/25 smoothing reserve was not drawn on because of underspends across all care groups.
findings.detail: Following an amendment on page 24 of the accounts, a sentence was added explaining that the smoothing reserve was not utilised due to underspend amongst all care groups.
findings.matters: A reserve held unused because of an underspend is a point finance directors compare across councils when judging how much cushion is held against future pressure.
findings.quote: the smoothing reserve was not utilised

findings.committee: Health and Social Care Partnership Integration Joint Board
findings.paper_title: Item 18b. Appendix 2 EO Performance Audit and Risk Committee Minutes 29.06.26
findings.headline: A reference to £2.804m in the 2024/25 accounts was changed to £2.755m of proposed savings, and the highest potential savings requirement was corrected from £11.7m to £12.7m.
findings.detail: The committee recorded post-audit amendments to the 2024/25 accounts. A second reference to £2.804m was updated to show proposed savings of £2.755m. A reference to £11.7m as the highest potential savings required was corrected to £12.7m.
findings.matters: Changes to the savings requirement and savings figures in published accounts show how a council's reported gap moved between draft and final, which matters to finance directors and lenders assessing the plan.
findings.quote: P27 (110) two references to £2.804m, second of which has been updated to reflect only proposed savings of £2.755m.

findings.committee: Health and Social Care Partnership Integration Joint Board
findings.paper_title: Item 18b. Appendix 2 EO Performance Audit and Risk Committee Minutes 29.06.26
findings.headline: Two of the four outstanding 2024/25 audit matters are rated medium risk, covering gross expenditure samples and quality and compliance checks.
findings.detail: The paper says the quality and compliance checks were assessed as medium risk, with the potential to result in a material adjustment or a significant change to disclosures in the financial statements. The remaining two outstanding matters were assessed as low risk.
findings.matters: Medium-risk open audit items that could change the financial statements are the kind of residual risk a finance director and a lender would want to see quantified.
findings.figures: 2 of 4 outstanding matters assessed as medium risk; 2 assessed as low risk
findings.quote: quality and compliance checks were assessed as medium risk, with the potential to result in a material adjustment or a significant change to disclosures within the financial statements.

findings.committee: Health and Social Care Partnership Integration Joint Board
findings.paper_title: Item 18b. Appendix 2 EO Performance Audit and Risk Committee Minutes 29.06.26
findings.headline: The 2024/25 IJB audit is substantially complete with 4 outstanding matters, and IT controls, previously outstanding, are now complete.
findings.detail: Forvis Mazars reported that the audit opinion remained substantially complete and that the IT controls identified as outstanding in the 9 June report are now complete. An additional matter was added, needing confirmation from the council's Legal Officer on claims or litigation affecting the IJB.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council or a lender would track whether an audit closes and how many open items remain before sign-off.
findings.quote: with final completion dependent on 4 outstanding matters.
